nodes.name: Ru-NiP electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The electrodeposition sample was conducted using a three-electrode system, where the pretreated Ni mesh as the working electrode, Ag/AgCl as the reference electrode, and a carbon rod as the counter electrode. For the deposition of Ru-NiP, the deposition bath contained NiCl2·6H2O (0.3 M), NaH2PO2·H2O (0.1 M), RuCl3·3H2O (0.01–0.15 M) and H3BO3 (0.5 M) (pH~3–5, controlled by 0.5 M H2SO4). The Ru-NiP catalysts were deposited on the Ni mesh conducted for 25 min at -30 mA/cm². After deposition was complete, the electrodes were rinsed with deionized water and vacuum-dried at 60 °C for 12 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-NiP shows dense film structure with ultrasmall Ru nanoclusters of average size 2.54±1.53 nm; SAED displays diffuse rings indicating amorphous nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1c shows the TEM image of Ru-NiP, which also illustrates the dense film structure. The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of Ru-NiP displays diffuse rings (Fig. 1d), suggesting its amorphous nature.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-NiP shows clear lattice fringes with spacing of 0.207 nm matching Ru (101) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images show clear lattice fringes with a spacing of 0.207 nm, matching the (101) plane of Ru (Fig. 1g and Fig. 1h).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-NiP elemental mappings show Ni, P, and Ru uniformly distributed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mappings obtained from the high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image (Fig. 1i) show that the Ni, P and Ru elements are uniformly distributed within the Ru-NiP electrocatalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru content in Ru-NiP is 1.03 wt%; in Ru-Ni is 2.23 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental analysis using TEM energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (STEM-EDX) confirms that the content of Ru was 1.03 wt% and 2.23 wt% respectively, uniformly distributed in the NiP and Ni supports (Fig. S9).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms Ru contents from STEM-EDX analysis (Table S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: These Ru contents were further confirmed through inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) testing (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-NiP shows amorphous characteristics; Ru-Ni shows alloying.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The amorphous characteristics of Ru-NiP and the alloying of Ru and Ni were also further verified by X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Fig. S10 and Fig. S11).

nodes.characterization_summary: Characteristic shifts in binding energies of Ni, P, and Ru elements demonstrate SMSI between Ru nanoclusters and amorphous NiP support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis revealed characteristic shifts in binding energies of Ni, P, and Ru elements (Fig. S10b-d and Figs. S12-13), demonstrating the SMSI between Ru nanoclusters and the amorphous NiP support.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES of Ru-NiP shows positive shift of near-edge adsorption energy and low white-line intensity vs Ru-Ni; broader delocalized WT contours; FT-EXAFS shows Ru-Ru at 2.42 Å with decreased intensity, Ru-O at 1.50 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) analysis revealed that Ru in Ru-NiP exhibits a positive shift in near-edge adsorption energy, along with a broader and delocalized wavelet transform (WT) contours compared to the Ru-Ni control sample... Ru-NiP exhibits a clear Ru-Ru coordination peak around 2.42 Å... shortened Ru-O bond pathway in Ru-NiP (1.50 Å).

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl: Ru-NiP 3.3 mF/cm² (ECSA 155 cm²), Ru-Ni 2.3 mF/cm² (88 cm²), NiP 1.7 mF/cm² (35 cm²), Ni 1.6 mF/cm² (22 cm²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl values for Ru-NiP, Ru-Ni, NiP and Ni were determined to be 3.3, 2.3, 1.7 and 1.6 mF/cm² (Fig. 2e and S25), resulting in the ECSA of 155, 88, 35 and 22 cm², respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-NiP(500h) shows similar Raman signal to pristine with slight increase in P-O-P band; Ru-Ni(500h) shows new Ni(OH)₂ peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru-NiP(500 h) exhibited a Raman signal similar to its original one, but with a slight increase in the Raman response of the P-O-P band... Ru-Ni(500 h) exhibited new peaks at 304, 465 and 1070 cm⁻¹, which are assigned to the E-type vibration mode of the Ni-OH lattice.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-NiP charge transfer resistance Rct = 0.94 Ω, significantly lower than Ru-Ni (2.09 Ω), NiP (4.07 Ω), Ni (17.05 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Nyquist plots obtained from the fitting analysis (Fig. 2c and S22), the charge transfer resistance (Rct) of Ru-NiP (0.94 Ω) is significantly lower than Ru-Ni (2.09 Ω), NiP (4.07Ω) and Ni (17.05 Ω).
